args.text:
Batch: 8 runs, all 8 accepted.
Flagged (6), reason other, likely duplicates: r01 with r07, r05 with r06, and r02 with r08. In each pair, the two runs have the same values for all three checks, every summary and the final settings. r02 and r08 also share the same kept remedy (registration from 400 px) and differ only in step count (5 vs 7).
Cleared (2): r03 and r04. All three checks pass, they don't copy any other run, their summaries are close to the batch, and r04's single kept remedy is the normal path.
What the flagged runs have in common: none failed a check. Each looks like one measurement reported under two run IDs, so I can't tell which root each one belongs to. Check how the runs were assigned to roots before using these results.
Note: the whole batch is unusually tight. The REGR peak is at 421 µm and the largest flank difference at 410 µm in every run, and the REGR peak spans only 52.75 to 52.92 %/h. The near-zero MADs are what make the z-scores look large. It's worth checking whether the cleared runs are truly separate roots.
